summary: Schmidt and Stix ask whether a variety is determined by its étale homotopy type X_et, an object of the homotopy category of Isaksen's model structure on pro-simplicial sets, rather than by its étale fundamental group alone. They reformulate Mochizuki's Hom theorem for hyperbolic curves over sub-p-adic fields without base points (Theorems 1.1 and 3.2). For varieties over a finitely generated field k/Q that embed in products of hyperbolic curves, they build a unique functorial retraction r of Isom_k(X, Y) → Isom_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et, Y_et) (Theorems 1.2 and 4.7). Mochizuki gives a morphism to the ambient product; Tamagawa's separation of rational points over finite fields and a point count in closed fibres (Propositions 4.1 and 4.6) show that it lands in the subvariety. Elements of the kernel of r act on π_1 by class-preserving automorphisms (Theorem 1.9, §5, via Čebotarev and ℓ-geometric covers of positive genus). For strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods, towers of elementary fibrations into hyperbolic curves, the kernel is trivial (Theorem 6.2), so these varieties are anabelian (Theorem 1.5, Corollary 1.6). Every point of a smooth variety has a basis of such neighbourhoods, as Grothendieck predicted (Lemma 6.3, Corollary 1.7). Pop's birational theorem gives absolute versions (Theorems 7.1–7.2). The appendix develops the needed homotopy theory of pro-spaces: coverings, base change along coverings, pointed versus unpointed maps, topological homotopy groups of profinite pro-spaces, and classifying spaces of pro-groups. The atlas plans a Mochizuki reconstruction theorem for proper hyperbolic curves over number fields (NC.1), étale cohomology and point counting (SF.2, EDC.2), resolution (R09.7), Hurwitz formulas and Kummer theory. It has nothing on étale homotopy types or pro-spaces, and nothing on higher-dimensional anabelian geometry. Routes: the homotopy theory of pro-spaces and étale homotopy types become a new roadmap, EtaleHomotopyTypes. The paper's own theorems become a Part II of Anabelian geometry and nonabelian Chabauty. The cited anabelian theorems (Mochizuki's Theorem A, Tamagawa, Pop, strongly center-free Galois groups) are sources of NC.1. Five further inputs go to IG.1, IG.2, AN.4, R09.2 and SF.0. Seven source issues are recorded, all present in the published text: six misprints, one of them the dropped word 'smooth' in Theorem 4.7(b), and one gap, where Proposition 5.5 applies Proposition 5.3 without checking r(γ′) = id.

items.name: Pro-objects and pro-categories
items.statement: A pro-object of a category C is a functor I^op → C from a small cofiltered (filtering) index category, written X = (X_i)_{i∈I}; pro-C has morphisms Mor(X, Y) = lim_j colim_i Mor_C(X_i, Y_j). Every pro-object is isomorphic to one indexed by a cofinite directed set (Edwards–Hastings 2.1.6).
items.locator: §1, Notation and conventions, p. 821; Appendix, p. 852
items.note: Mathlib has no pro-category of a general category at 082e2d3 (DiamondsAndVStacks D0 plans pro-categories only of the small categories it needs).

items.name: Simplicial sets, nerves, Kan complexes and model categories
items.statement: Simplicial sets and pointed simplicial sets, the nerve of a small category, the standard simplices and horns, Kan complexes, and the notion of a (closed) model category.
items.note: Mathlib: SSet, SSet.stdSimplex, SSet.horn, SSet.KanComplex (Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialSet/*), CategoryTheory.nerve, HomotopicalAlgebra.ModelCategory (Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/ModelCategory/Basic.lean).

items.name: Homotopy groups of simplicial sets and classifying spaces of discrete groups
items.statement: Homotopy groups π_n of pointed (Kan) simplicial sets; for a discrete group G the nerve BG of its one-object category is a K(G,1) with π_1(BG) = G, EG → BG is a G-covering with EG contractible, and a surjection G′ → G induces a fibration BG′ → BG, so BG is fibrant.
items.note: Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology Stage 8 plans homotopy groups of Kan simplicial sets; StableHomotopyKTheory H.1 plans nerves, classifying spaces and K(G,1) identification.

items.name: Isaksen's model structure on pro-simplicial sets
items.statement: The strict (Isaksen) closed simplicial model structure on pro-ss and its pointed variant pro-ss_*, with every object cofibrant; its homotopy category Ho(pro-ss), with Mor_Ho(X, Y) the strict simplicial homotopy classes of maps into a fibrant Y (Hirschhorn 9.5.24); weak equivalences detected on π_0 and on the pro-homotopy groups (Isaksen Cor. 7.5); strong fibrations are fibrations (Isaksen 14.5); the structure is proper (Isaksen 17.1 with the correction [Isa04] 4.14); and the cohomological criterion for weak equivalences (Isaksen 18.4; Artin–Mazur 4.3).
items.note: The whole homotopy theory of pro-spaces used in the paper; nothing in the atlas or the pinned libraries plans it.

items.name: Étale topological type and étale homotopy groups
items.statement: For a locally noetherian scheme X, X_et ∈ pro-ss is obtained by applying the connected-component functor to the cofiltered system of rigid étale hypercovers (Friedlander). A geometric point x̄ gives a point x̄_et, and π_n^et(X, x̄) := π_n(X_et, x̄_et). For X locally noetherian, π_1^et is the SGA 3 X §6 étale fundamental group, whose profinite completion is the SGA 1 group; if X is noetherian and geometrically unibranch these pro-groups are profinite (Artin–Mazur 11.1). For a field k, G_k = π_1(k_et, K_et).
items.note: Uses rigid hypercovers of the étale site (SF.2) and the SGA 1 fundamental group (IG.0).

items.name: Étale homotopy exact sequence for a geometric fibration (Friedlander, Thm. 11.5)
items.statement: For a morphism f: X → Y of geometrically unibranch schemes that is an elementary fibration (more generally, satisfies Friedlander's hypotheses), with the pull-back 𝒳 of the system of pointed Galois covers of (Y, ȳ), there is a long exact sequence ⋯ → π_n^et(X_ȳ, x̄) → π_n^et(𝒳) → π_n^et(𝒴) → π_{n−1}^et(X_ȳ, x̄) → ⋯.
items.note: Cited from Friedlander, Étale homotopy of simplicial schemes, Thm. 11.5, with L the set of all primes.

items.name: Remark 1.4(2): étale realization factors through A¹-homotopy theory
items.statement: By Isaksen (Adv. Math. 2004) the functor X ↦ X_et from smooth k-schemes to Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et factors through the Morel–Voevodsky A¹-homotopy category; in particular it is not faithful.
items.note: Not used in the proofs; recorded as the reason Theorem 1.2 needs A¹-local schemes.

items.name: Lemma 2.1: finite étale morphisms give finite coverings of étale types
items.statement: If p: W′ → W is finite étale, then p_et: W′_et → W_et is a finite covering in pro-ss, and for any X → W the natural map (X ×_W W′)_et → X_et ×_{W_et} W′_et is an isomorphism in pro-ss.

items.name: Lemma 2.2: base change of homotopy equivalences along finite étale maps
items.statement: Let f: X → W, g: Y → W and γ ∈ Isom_Ho(pro-ss)(X_et, Y_et) with g_et γ = f_et. For W′ → W finite étale there is γ′ ∈ Isom_Ho(pro-ss)((X ×_W W′)_et, (Y ×_W W′)_et) compatible with γ and with the projections to W′_et (γ′ is not asserted to be unique).
items.note: From Lemma 2.1 and Proposition A.6.

items.name: Proposition 2.3: Galois-equivariant comparison of geometric cohomology
items.statement: Let X, Y be varieties over k with X_et ≅ Y_et in Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et. Then there are G_k-isomorphisms H^i_et(X_k̄, A) ≅ H^i_et(Y_k̄, A), functorial in the abelian group A, for all i ≥ 0.
items.note: The proof identifies (X ×_k k̄)_et with X_et ×_{k_et} (k′_et)_{k′⊂k̄} via limits of étale cohomology and the cohomological criterion, then applies Proposition A.6.

items.name: Strongly center-free profinite groups; sub-p-adic fields (Mochizuki, Lemma 15.8)
items.statement: A profinite group is strongly center-free if every open subgroup has trivial center. A sub-p-adic field is a subfield of a finitely generated extension of Q_p. Absolute Galois groups of sub-p-adic fields (in particular of finitely generated extensions of Q) are strongly center-free (Mochizuki, Invent. Math. 138 (1999), Lemma 15.8).
items.note: Proved in Mochizuki's local pro-p anabelian paper; it belongs with the Mochizuki reconstruction theorem.

items.name: Proposition 2.4: pointed versus unpointed morphisms of étale types over k
items.statement: Ho(pro-ss) is the homotopy category of Isaksen's model structure on pro-simplicial sets; Ho(pro-ss)↓B is the category of morphisms to B in it; X_et is the étale topological type of X. Let X, Y be connected k-varieties, Y geometrically unibranch and geometrically connected, and x̄, ȳ geometric points over a separably closed K/k. (a) Forgetting base points gives a surjection Mor_{Ho(pro-ss_*)↓(k_et, k̄_et)}((X_et, x̄_et), (Y_et, ȳ_et)) ↠ Mor_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et, Y_et); in particular isomorphic unpointed types are isomorphic pointed. (b) It factors through the orbits of π_1^et(Y_k̄, ȳ). (c) If G_k is strongly center-free, the induced map on π_1^et(Y_k̄, ȳ)-orbits is a bijection.
items.note: From Theorems A.8, A.13 and Lemma A.12.

items.name: Corollaries 2.5–2.6: induced outer homomorphisms and π₁-open maps
items.statement: For X, Y as in Proposition 2.4, OutHom_{G_k}(π_1^et(X), π_1^et(Y)) := Hom_{G_k}(π_1^et(X, x̄), π_1^et(Y, ȳ))_{π_1^et(Y_k̄, ȳ)} is independent of base points, and Mor_k(X, Y) → OutHom_{G_k} factors through Mor_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et, Y_et) when G_k is strongly center-free (Corollary 2.5). With Mor^{π_1-open} the maps whose π_1 has open image, the pointed π_1-open maps modulo π_1^et(Y_k̄, ȳ) biject with the unpointed π_1-open maps (Corollary 2.6).

items.name: Varieties of type K(π,1) and Lemma 2.7
items.statement: A geometrically pointed connected locally noetherian scheme (X, x̄) is of type K(π,1) if π_n^et(X, x̄) = 0 for all n ≥ 2, equivalently the classifying morphism (X_et, x̄_et) → Bπ_1(X_et, x̄_et) is an isomorphism in Ho(pro-ss_*); for geometrically unibranch X this is independent of the base point. Lemma 2.7: (1) a connected smooth curve over a field that is affine or of genus > 0 is of type K(π,1) (Schmidt, Compositio 1996, Prop. 15); (2) over a characteristic-zero field a product of geometrically connected, geometrically unibranch varieties of type K(π,1) is of type K(π,1).
items.note: Part (2) uses the Künneth formulas for π_1 (SGA 1 XIII 4.6) and étale cohomology, and the cohomological criterion (Artin–Mazur 4.3).

items.name: Proposition 2.8: elementary fibrations preserve K(π,1)
items.statement: An elementary fibration X → Y is the complement, in a smooth proper curve X̄ → Y with geometrically connected fibres, of a divisor D finite étale over Y with affine fibres X → Y. Over a field of characteristic zero, if f: X → Y is an elementary fibration of smooth varieties and Y is of type K(π,1), then X is of type K(π,1), and 1 → π_1^et(X_ȳ) → π_1^et(X) → π_1^et(Y) → 1 is exact.

items.name: Existence of Artin's good neighbourhoods (SGA 4 XI 3.3)
items.statement: For a smooth variety X of dimension d with a projective compactification X ⊆ X̄ ⊆ P(V) (X̄ normal, O(1)|_X̄ an r-th multiple, r ≥ 2), the linear projections from general Δ_W, W ∈ Grass_d(V), restricted over a non-empty open S_W ⊆ P(W), are elementary fibrations U_W → S_W; over an algebraically closed field every point lies in some U_W.
items.note: The paper applies SGA 4 XI 3.3 over an infinite perfect field at a rational point, then descends from k̄ to k.

items.name: Lemma 2.9: maps into products of K(π,1) varieties are componentwise
items.statement: Let k have characteristic zero with G_k strongly center-free, X a k-variety and Y_1, Y_2 geometrically connected, geometrically unibranch k-varieties of type K(π,1). Then Hom_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et, (Y_1 ×_k Y_2)_et) → Hom(X_et, Y_{1,et}) × Hom(X_et, Y_{2,et}) is bijective.

items.name: Künneth formula for étale fundamental groups in characteristic zero (SGA 1 XIII 4.6)
items.statement: For geometrically connected varieties Y_1, Y_2 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, π_1^et(Y_1 × Y_2) ≅ π_1^et(Y_1) × π_1^et(Y_2); hence over any characteristic-zero k, π_1^et(Y_1 ×_k Y_2) ≅ π_1^et(Y_1) ×_{G_k} π_1^et(Y_2).
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 2.7(2) and Lemma 2.9, pp. 827–828
items.note: IG.1 keeps the geometric/arithmetic fundamental-group sequence in the selected SGA range.

items.name: Künneth formula for étale cohomology (SGA 4½, Th. finitude, Cor. 1.11)
items.statement: For varieties over an algebraically closed field and torsion coefficients prime to the characteristic, the étale cohomology of a product is computed by the Künneth formula.
items.note: SF.2 integrates the CohomologicalPointCounting (PR196) suppliers, which provide Künneth/base change/Leray (cited by DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.6).

items.name: Definition A.1: coverings and Galois coverings of pro-spaces
items.statement: A map of simplicial sets p: Y → X is a covering if every Δ[0] → Y over Δ[n] → X lifts uniquely (Gabriel–Zisman); coverings lift uniquely against horns and are fibrations; a connected covering is Galois with group Aut_X(Y) if Y/Aut_X(Y) ≅ X. A morphism of pro-spaces is a covering (resp. Galois covering) if it is isomorphic to a level-wise one. A pointed connected pro-space has a pointed universal covering (the system of level-wise universal coverings), which is Galois with group π_1(X, x).

items.name: Proposition A.2: the covering associated with a sub-pro-group
items.statement: For (X, x) connected in Ho(pro-ss_*) and a monomorphism of pro-groups U ↪ π_1(X, x), there is (X, x)_U → (X, x) in Ho(pro-ss_*)_c such that for every connected (W, w), [(W, w), (X, x)_U] ≅ {f ∈ [(W, w), (X, x)] : π_1(f) factors through U}.
items.note: Proved as Artin–Mazur §2 (2.7), (2.8).

items.name: Lemmas A.3–A.5: coverings, fibrations and properness
items.statement: Lemma A.3: pull-back along a weak equivalence of connected pro-spaces is an equivalence of categories of connected coverings. Lemma A.4: coverings are fibrations in pro-ss. Lemma A.5: for a fibration W′ → W and a weak equivalence h: Y → X over W, h × id: Y ×_W W′ → X ×_W W′ is a weak equivalence (properness; Hirschhorn 13.3.2).

items.name: Proposition A.6: base change of homotopy equivalences along coverings
items.statement: Let f: X → W, g: Y → W be maps of pro-spaces and γ ∈ Isom_Ho(pro-ss)(X, Y) with gγ = f. For a covering W′ → W there is γ′ ∈ Isom_Ho(pro-ss)(X ×_W W′, Y ×_W W′) compatible with γ and the projections to W′, functorial in W′; for a Galois covering of connected pro-spaces the induced isomorphisms H^i(Y ×_W W′, A) → H^i(X ×_W W′, A) are G(W′/W)-equivariant.

items.name: Lemma A.7: derived limits of profinite pro-groups vanish
items.statement: For a pro-finite group G = (G_i), lim¹ G = * (Bousfield–Kan's non-abelian lim¹); for a pro-finite abelian group, lim^s G = 0 for all s ≥ 1.
items.note: Via the strongly Mittag-Leffler pro-group G*_i = ∏_{j≤i} G_j and compactness.

items.name: Theorem A.8: topological homotopy groups of profinite pro-spaces
items.statement: Define π_n^top(X, x) := π_n(holim X) = Mor_{Ho(pro-ss_*)}((S^n, s_n), (X, x)) and call (X, x) path-connected if π_0^top = *. If π_0(X, x) = * and all π_n(X, x) are pro-finite, then π_n^top(X, x) → lim π_n(X, x) is an isomorphism for all n ≥ 0.
items.note: By the Bousfield–Kan spectral sequence of the cosimplicial replacement and Lemma A.7.

items.name: Lemma A.9, Theorem A.10 and Corollary A.11: pointed versus unpointed classes
items.statement: Paths in a fibrant approximation give a well-defined associative action π_1^top(Y, y_0, y_1) × [(X, x), (Y, y_0)]_* → [(X, x), (Y, y_1)]_* (Lemma A.9). If Y is path-connected, forgetting base points induces a bijection ([(X, x), (Y, y)]_*)_{π_1^top(Y, y)} ≅ [X, Y] (Theorem A.10). If X ≅ Y in Ho(pro-ss) and all π_i(Y, y) are pro-finite, then (X, x) ≅ (Y, y) in Ho(pro-ss_*) (Corollary A.11).
items.locator: Lemma A.9, Theorem A.10 and Corollary A.11, p. 859
items.note: The paper says Theorem A.10 is proved 'formally in the same way' as for well-pointed spaces (Whitehead III §1) and gives no further proof.

items.name: Lemma A.12: the monodromy action is conjugation on π₁
items.statement: For pointed connected pro-spaces, the π_1^top(Y, y)-action on Hom(π_1^top(X, x), π_1^top(Y, y)) induced by α ↦ α(id_Y) is φ ↦ α φ(−) α^{−1}; the orbits are the outer homomorphisms.

items.name: Theorem A.13: pointed versus unpointed over a base
items.statement: Let (X, x), (Y, y) be pointed pro-spaces over (B, b) with Y, B path-connected and π_1^top(Y, y) → π_1^top(B, b) surjective. (a) Forgetting base points gives a surjection Mor_{Ho(pro-ss_*)↓(B,b)}((X, x), (Y, y)) ↠ Mor_{Ho(pro-ss)↓B}(X, Y), and isomorphisms lift to isomorphisms. (b) With S_X ⊆ π_1^top(B, b) the stabilizer of the structure map of (X, x) and Δ_{X,Y} its preimage in π_1^top(Y, y), the map on Δ_{X,Y}-orbits is a bijection.
items.locator: Theorem A.13, p. 860; proof as corrected by E5

items.name: Pro-classifying spaces: BG, EG and the fibrant model B*G (Lemma A.14)
items.statement: For a pro-group G, BG and EG are defined level-wise; EG is contractible and EG_i → BG_i is a G_i-covering, but BG need not be fibrant. With G* = (∏_{j≤i} G_j)_i and B*G := EG*/G, B*G is fibrant in pro-ss_* and BG → B*G is a weak equivalence (Lemma A.14).

items.name: Lemma A.15 and Proposition A.16: BG represents Hom(π₁(−), G)
items.statement: For pro-groups G, G′, the maps Hom(G′, G) → Hom_{pro-ss_*}(BG′, BG) → Hom_{Ho(pro-ss_*)}(BG′, BG) → Hom(G′, G) are all bijections (Lemma A.15). For a connected pointed pro-space (X, x) and a pro-group G, π_1(−): Mor_{Ho(pro-ss_*)}((X, x), BG) → Mor_{pro-groups}(π_1(X, x), G) is a functorial bijection (Proposition A.16).
items.locator: Lemma A.15 and Proposition A.16, pp. 863–864
items.note: Uses the fundamental groupoid nerve BΠX and the level-wise covering B*G → BG*.

items.name: Definition A.17 and Corollary A.18: classifying morphism and K(π,1) pro-spaces
items.statement: The classifying morphism of a pointed connected pro-space is the map (X, x) → Bπ_1(X, x) in Ho(pro-ss_*) corresponding to the identity of π_1 under Proposition A.16; (X, x) is of type K(π,1) if π_i(X, x) = 0 for i ≥ 2, which holds iff the classifying morphism is an isomorphism (Corollary A.18, via Isaksen Cor. 7.5).
items.locator: Definition A.17 and Corollary A.18, p. 866

items.name: Hyperbolic curves and the conventions of the paper
items.statement: All schemes are separated and locally noetherian; an immersion is an open followed by a closed immersion; an étale covering is a finite étale morphism; a variety is a scheme of finite type over a field. A hyperbolic curve over k is a geometrically connected (smooth) curve C with χ(C_k̄, Q_ℓ) < 0, i.e. 2g − 2 + n > 0 for genus g and n geometric boundary points.
items.note: NC.1 plans only smooth proper hyperbolic curves over number fields; the affine hyperbolic curves over general fields used throughout are part of the new Part II's carrier.

items.name: Theorem 3.1: Mochizuki's Hom theorem for sub-p-adic fields (Theorem A)
items.statement: Let k be sub-p-adic, X a smooth connected k-variety and Y a smooth hyperbolic curve over k. For any geometric base points, Mor_k^dom(X, Y) → Mor^open_{G_k}(π_1^et(X, x̄), π_1^et(Y, ȳ))_{π_1^et(Y_k̄, ȳ)} is bijective, where Mor^dom are dominant k-morphisms and Mor^open_{G_k} are continuous G_k-homomorphisms with open image.
items.locator: Theorem 3.1, p. 829 (Mochizuki, Invent. Math. 138 (1999), Thm. A)
items.note: NC.1 plans a Mochizuki reconstruction theorem for smooth proper hyperbolic curves over number fields and states that the Hom version and the affine variants need their own sources; this is that source. Also used over the function field of Y in Theorem 6.2.

items.name: Tamagawa: distinct rational points have non-conjugate decomposition groups (Cor. 2.10)
items.statement: Let C be a smooth proper curve of genus ≥ 1 over a finite field F. The decomposition subgroups in π_1^et(C) of distinct F-rational points are not conjugate; consequently for each w ∈ C(F) there is a connected étale covering C′ → C, geometrically connected, with an F-point over w and none over any other F-point of C.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.6, pp. 834–835 (Tamagawa, Compositio 109 (1997), Cor. 2.10)
items.note: The step from non-conjugacy to an open subgroup excluding all conjugates of the other decomposition groups is a compactness argument the paper leaves implicit. A finite-field variant of the reconstruction theory that NC.1 asks to be sourced separately.

items.name: Pop's birational anabelian theorem for finitely generated fields over Q
items.statement: For finitely generated extension fields k, ℓ of Q, Isom(Spec k, Spec ℓ) → OutIsom(G_k, G_ℓ) ≅ Isom_Ho(pro-ss)(k_et, ℓ_et) is a bijection (Pop, Ann. of Math. 139 (1994); Pop, Progr. Math. 181 (2000)).
items.note: The field-reconstruction case of source-qualified anabelian reconstruction; nothing in the atlas plans it.

items.name: Galois groups of Hilbertian fields have no nontrivial finitely generated closed normal subgroups
items.statement: Finitely generated extensions of Q are Hilbertian, and the absolute Galois group of a Hilbertian field has no nontrivial finitely generated closed normal subgroup (Fried–Jarden, Field Arithmetic, 3rd ed., Prop. 16.11.6).
items.note: IG.2 owns Hilbert irreducibility; PAPER-BRESCIANI-24 marks Hilbertian fields as planned there.

items.name: Finite generation of geometric fundamental groups in characteristic zero
items.statement: For a geometrically connected variety X over a field k of characteristic zero, π_1^et(X_k̄, x̄) = ker(π_1^et(X, x̄) → G_k) is topologically finitely generated (cited as SGA 7 II Thm. 2.3.1 in the paper; classically SGA 1 XII via Riemann existence).
items.note: IG.1 owns the arithmetic exact sequence; PAPER-BRESCIANI-24 routes the finitely generated curve-fibre groups there.

items.name: Čebotarev density for schemes of finite type over Z (Serre, Thm. 7)
items.statement: For a finite étale Galois covering 𝒴 → 𝒳 with group G of a scheme of finite type over Z, every element of G is the Frobenius of some closed point, and the covering is determined by its set of totally split closed points: for two such coverings one dominates the other iff the split set of the first is contained in that of the second, up to a set of density zero.
items.note: AN.4 keeps Chebotarev and prime-ideal applications (after RS-07); this is the arithmetic-scheme version of Serre, Zeta and L functions (1965), Thm. 7.

items.name: Closed points of schemes of finite type over Z: Jacobson property and finite residue fields
items.statement: A scheme of finite type over Z is Jacobson, so a reduced such scheme is covered by the closures of its closed points, and every closed point has a finite residue field (EGA IV 10.4.6 and 10.4.11.1).
items.note: Mathlib has AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace and MvPolynomial.comp_C_integral_of_surjective_of_isJacobsonRing, but no IsJacobsonRing ℤ instance and no finite-residue-field statement; the adapter is general scheme theory.

items.name: Spreading out over a regular base of finite type over Z
items.statement: Given finitely many varieties, morphisms, immersions, smooth compactifications with strict normal crossing boundary and finite étale coverings over a finitely generated field k/Q, there is a regular connected scheme S of finite type over Z with function field k over which all of them extend with the same properties.
items.locator: Proofs of Propositions 4.4, 5.1 and Lemma 5.2, pp. 833, 839–840
items.note: The standard EGA IV §8 limit arguments, used without statement in the paper.

items.name: Resolution of singularities and normal-crossings compactification in characteristic zero
items.statement: Over a field of characteristic zero, smooth varieties X, Y with morphisms to a proper W have smooth compactifications X̄, Ȳ with simple normal crossing boundary to which the morphisms extend.
items.note: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.7 plans characteristic-zero resolution and normal-crossings compactification.

items.name: Relative purity for a strict normal crossing divisor
items.statement: For j: X ↪ X̄ the complement of a relative strict normal crossing divisor D = ∪ D_α over S and ℓ invertible on S, R^b j_* Q_ℓ = Λ^b R^1 j_* Q_ℓ ≅ ⊕_{|J|=b} i_{J,*} Q_ℓ(−b) (Gabber's work, Exp. XVI Cor. 3.1.3).
items.note: EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.2 plans the smooth trace and relative purity.

items.name: Smooth and proper base change, and local constancy of higher direct images
items.statement: For proper smooth morphisms the sheaves R^a f_* Q_ℓ are smooth (SGA 4½ Arcata V 3.1); smooth sheaves on a normal connected S give π_1^et(S)-representations with cospecialisation isomorphisms, and compactly supported cohomology commutes with base change.
items.note: SF.2 plans proper/smooth base change and compact support.

items.name: Poincaré duality for smooth varieties
items.statement: For X smooth of pure dimension d over a separably closed field, H^i(X, Q_ℓ) × H^{2d−i}_c(X, Q_ℓ) → Q_ℓ(−d) is a perfect Galois-equivariant pairing.
items.note: EDC.2 plans Poincaré duality.

items.name: Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula
items.statement: For X of finite type over a finite field F_s, |X(F_s)| = Σ_i (−1)^i tr(Frob_s | H^i_c(X_s̄, Q_ℓ)).
items.note: As in PAPER-WOOD-19, the trace formula for rational point counts is planned in SF.2 (integrating CohomologicalPointCounting).

items.name: Lifting étale coverings from a closed fibre to a Nisnevich neighbourhood
items.statement: Let W → S be proper and s ∈ S closed. Every finite étale covering of W_s extends to a finite étale covering of W_T for some Nisnevich neighbourhood (T, t) → (S, s) (the paper cites Artin, Publ. IHÉS 36, Thm. 3.1).
items.note: Over the henselization this is the SGA 1 X specialization of covers for proper W; a limit argument then descends to a Nisnevich neighbourhood. IG.1 keeps the specialization maps for smooth proper families.

items.name: Riemann–Hurwitz for tame coverings of curves
items.statement: For a finite covering of smooth curves that is at most tamely ramified along the boundary of smooth compactifications, the Euler characteristic 2g − 2 + n is multiplicative in the degree.
items.note: Tau Ceti AlgebraicCurves Layer 7 plans the Hurwitz genus formula.

items.name: Elementary abelian ℓ-coverings of the projective line minus n points
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (or prime to ℓ), the Galois group of the maximal elementary abelian ℓ-covering of P¹ minus n ≥ 1 points is F_ℓ^{n−1}, and the inertia groups of the n boundary points are pairwise distinct lines.
items.note: IG.3 plans branched covers from generating tuples with product one via Riemann existence.

items.name: Isom schemes of elementary fibrations in hyperbolic curves are finite unramified
items.statement: For an elementary fibration X → Y in hyperbolic curves, the Isom scheme Isom(X/Y, X/Y) → Y is finite and unramified (Deligne–Mumford, Thm. 1.11), so a K-point at the generic point extends uniquely to a Y-point.
items.note: R09.2 develops relative Hom and Isom schemes where moduli proofs invoke them; finiteness and unramifiedness for stable (hyperbolic) curves is that input.

items.name: Kummer theory for Galois cohomology
items.statement: For a field k of characteristic zero, H^1(k, μ_n) ≅ k^×/(k^×)^n, naturally in k.
items.note: Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9 plans Hilbert 90 and Kummer theory.

items.name: Profinite groups, absolute Galois groups and compactness arguments
items.statement: Absolute Galois groups with the Krull topology, open and closed subgroups, continuous homomorphisms of profinite groups, and the compactness principle that a decreasing family of nonempty closed subsets of a profinite space has nonempty intersection.
items.locator: §1, p. 821; proofs of Lemma 5.2, Proposition 5.3, Lemma 5.6, pp. 840–844
items.note: Mathlib: Field.absoluteGaloisGroup, krullTopology, ProfiniteGrp, IsCompact.nonempty_iInter_of_directed_nonempty_isCompact_isClosed.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 3.2: Mochizuki's theorem in homotopy form
items.statement: Theorem 3.2: for k sub-p-adic, X a smooth connected k-variety and Y a smooth hyperbolic curve over k, Mor_k^dom(X, Y) → Mor^{π_1-open}_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et, Y_et) is bijective. Theorem 1.1: for hyperbolic curves X, Y over k, Isom_k(X, Y) → Isom_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et, Y_et) is bijective.
items.locator: Theorem 1.1, p. 818; Theorem 3.2 and proof, pp. 829–830
items.note: From Theorem 3.1, Proposition 2.4 and Proposition A.16 (hyperbolic curves are K(π,1) by Lemma 2.7).

items.name: Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 1.3: the retraction
items.statement: Let k be finitely generated over Q and X, Y smooth geometrically connected k-varieties that embed as locally closed subschemes in products of hyperbolic curves. Then Isom_k(X, Y) → Isom_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et, Y_et) is a split injection with a functorial retraction r (Theorem 1.2). In particular X_et ≅ Y_et in Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et implies X ≅ Y (Corollary 1.3).
items.note: Proved as Theorem 4.7.

items.name: Proposition 4.1: point counts in closed fibres from generic-fibre cohomology
items.statement: Let S be normal noetherian, s ∈ S closed with finite residue field F_s of size N(s), ℓ invertible on S, X̄ → S proper smooth of relative dimension d and X ⊆ X̄ the complement of a relative strict normal crossing divisor with smooth components. Then the G_{κ(η)}-action on H^i(X_η̄, Q_ℓ) factors through π_1^et(S, η̄), and |X_s(F_s)| = N(s)^d Σ_{i=0}^{2d} (−1)^i tr(φ_s | H^i_et(X_η̄, Q_ℓ)), with φ_s the arithmetic Frobenius.
items.note: Assembles relative purity, Leray, smooth and proper base change, Poincaré duality and the trace formula (the planned items above); checked on A¹ and G_m.

items.name: Definition 4.2: factor-dominant immersions
items.statement: An immersion ι: Y ↪ W = C_1 × ⋯ × C_n into a product of smooth geometrically connected curves is factor-dominant if every p_i ι is dominant. For Y geometrically connected and geometrically reduced each p_i ι is dominant or constant with k-rational image, so constant factors can be removed.

items.name: Proposition 4.3: morphisms to the ambient product from étale types
items.statement: Let k be sub-p-adic, ι: Y ↪ W = C_1 × ⋯ × C_n a factor-dominant immersion of a geometrically connected, geometrically unibranch k-variety into a product of hyperbolic curves, and X smooth connected. For every π_1-open γ: X_et → Y_et in Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et there is a unique k-morphism f: X → W with f_et = ι_et γ.
items.note: From Theorem 3.2 and Lemma 2.9.

items.name: Proposition 4.4 and Remark 4.5: the morphism factors through Y
items.statement: Let k be finitely generated over Q, ι: Y ↪ W a smooth locally closed subscheme of a product of hyperbolic curves, X smooth and f: X → W with f_et = ι_et γ for some γ ∈ Isom_Ho(pro-ss)(X_et, Y_et). Then f = ι g for a unique g: X → Y. (Remark 4.5: g_et also satisfies the diagram, but γ = g_et is not claimed.)
items.note: Reduces to Proposition 4.6 after passing to covers with genus ≥ 2 compactifications, compactifying and spreading out.

items.name: Proposition 4.6: Tamagawa's point-count argument
items.statement: Let S be regular connected of finite type over Z, C_i → S proper smooth curves with geometrically connected fibres of genus ≥ 1, ι: Y ↪ W = ∏_S C_i a locally closed subscheme smooth over S, and f: X → W an S-morphism with X/S smooth, where X and Y have nice relative compactifications mapping to W. If (f_η)_et = (ι_η)_et γ for some γ ∈ Isom_Ho(pro-ss)((X_η)_et, (Y_η)_et), then f factors through Y.
items.note: Checked: for x ∈ X(F), a covering W′ → W with W′_s(F) = {f(x)} and Proposition 4.1 give |Y′_s(F)| = q^{d_Y − d_X}|X′_s(F)| > 0.

items.name: Theorem 4.7: the unique functorial retraction
items.statement: For k finitely generated over Q and X, Y smooth geometrically connected varieties embeddable in products of hyperbolic curves, (−)_et: Isom_k(X, Y) → Isom_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et, Y_et) admits a unique functorial retraction r such that (a) r(g_et) = g for every k-isomorphism g; (b) r(γ_2 γ_1) = r(γ_2) r(γ_1) for a further smooth geometrically connected such Z; and (c) h_et r(γ)_et = h_et γ for every dominant h: Y → C to a hyperbolic curve. r(γ) is independent of the chosen immersion.
items.locator: Theorem 4.7, pp. 835–837; statement and proof as corrected by E1–E2
items.note: r(γ) is built from Propositions 4.3–4.4; it is an isomorphism formally from (a) and (b).

items.name: Proposition 4.8: compatibility of r with dominant maps
items.statement: For X, X′, Y, Y′ as in Theorem 4.7, dominant k-morphisms f: X′ → X, g: Y′ → Y and isomorphisms γ′, γ with γ f_et = g_et γ′, one has g r(γ′) = r(γ) f.

items.name: Theorem 1.9 and class-preserving automorphisms
items.statement: For 1 → H → G → Γ → 1, φ ∈ Aut_Γ(G) is class-preserving by elements of H if φ(g) ∈ {hgh^{−1} : h ∈ H} for every g. Theorem 1.9: for k finitely generated over Q, X smooth geometrically connected and embeddable in a product of hyperbolic curves, and γ in the kernel of r: Aut_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et) → Aut_k(X), the outer automorphism π_1(γ) ∈ OutAut_{G_k}(π_1^et(X)) is class-preserving by elements of π_1^et(X_k̄).
items.note: Assembled from Propositions 5.1, 5.3, 5.5 and Lemma 5.6.

items.name: Proposition 5.1: normality under hypothesis (NR)
items.statement: Let X be as in Theorem 1.9 with a factor-dominant immersion ι: X ↪ ∏ C_i such that (NR) no C_i is rational. For γ ∈ Aut_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et) with r(γ) = id_X, φ = π_1(γ) maps every open normal subgroup N of π_1^et(X) to itself.
items.note: Via ι_et γ = ι_et, Proposition A.2, Čebotarev for schemes and the argument of Proposition 4.6 applied to X_N and X_φ(N).

items.name: Lemma 5.2: automorphisms send elements to conjugates of powers
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 5.1, a pointed lift φ ∈ Aut_{G_k}(π_1^et(X, x̄)) satisfies φ(g) = h_g g^{m(g)} h_g^{−1} with h_g ∈ π_1^et(X, x̄) and m(g) ∈ Ẑ^× for every g.
items.note: In each finite quotient via Čebotarev (Frobenius elements and decomposition groups), then a compactness argument.

items.name: Proposition 5.3: class preservation under (NR)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 5.1, φ is class-preserving: every element of π_1^et(X, x̄) is mapped to a conjugate.
items.locator: Proposition 5.3, p. 841; proof as corrected by E4
items.note: m(g) = 1 whenever the image of g under π_1^et(X) → G_k → Ẑ (a Ẑ-quotient of the cyclotomic character) generates an open subgroup; these elements are dense.

items.name: Lemma 5.4: ℓ-geometric covers of positive genus exhaust π₁ of a hyperbolic curve
items.statement: A connected pointed étale covering h: (X′, x̄′) → (X, x̄) is ℓ-geometric if π_1^et(X_k̄, x̄) acts on h^{−1}(x̄) through a finite ℓ-group. For ℓ ≠ char k and (C, c̄) a hyperbolic curve over k, π_1^et(C, c̄) is the union of the open subgroups H for which C_H → C is ℓ-geometric and C_H has smooth compactification of genus ≥ 1.
items.note: Checked the count: n_H ≤ (d/ℓ)(n − 1) + d with Riemann–Hurwitz gives 2g(C_H) − 2 ≥ (d/ℓ)((ℓ − 1)(n − 3) − 2) ≥ 1 once n ≥ 6.

items.name: Proposition 5.5: class preservation in general
items.statement: Let k be finitely generated over Q and X smooth geometrically connected, embeddable in a product of hyperbolic curves. For γ ∈ Aut_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et) with r(γ) = id_X, π_1(γ) ∈ OutAut_{G_k}(π_1(X)) is class-preserving.
items.locator: Proposition 5.5, pp. 843–844; proof as completed by E6
items.note: Rational factors are replaced by ℓ-geometric covers of positive genus containing the image of a given σ (Lemma 5.4, with ℓ larger than the index of a normal subgroup in the image of π_1(X), so X′ stays geometrically connected).

items.name: Lemma 5.6: class preservation by elements of the kernel
items.statement: Let 1 → Ḡ → G → Γ → 1 be an exact sequence of profinite groups and φ ∈ Aut_Γ(G). If for every open Γ′ ⊆ Γ the induced φ′ ∈ Aut_{Γ′}(p^{−1}(Γ′)) is class-preserving, then φ is class-preserving by elements of Ḡ.

items.name: Definition 6.1: strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods
items.statement: A strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhood over k is a smooth k-variety X with a tower X = X_n → ⋯ → X_1 → X_0 = Spec k in which each X_i → X_{i−1} is an elementary fibration into hyperbolic curves and each X_i embeds into a product of hyperbolic curves. Example: M_{0,n}, n ≥ 4 (forget points one at a time; forget all but four points in all ways). Over characteristic 0 they are of type K(π,1) by Proposition 2.8.

items.name: Theorem 6.2: the retraction is injective on strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods
items.statement: Let k be finitely generated over Q and X a strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhood over k. If γ ∈ Aut_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et) has r(γ) = id_X, then γ = id_{X_et}.
items.locator: Theorem 6.2, pp. 845–847; proof as corrected by E3
items.note: Induction along the tower: the induced δ on the base has r(δ) = id by Proposition 4.8; on the generic fibre Mochizuki's Theorem A gives g_η, which extends through the finite unramified Isom scheme.

items.name: Theorem 1.5 and Corollary 1.6: anabelian strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods
items.statement: For strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods X, Y over k finitely generated over Q, Isom_k(X, Y) → Isom_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et, Y_et) is bijective (Theorem 1.5), equivalently Isom_k(X, Y) → OutIsom_{G_k}(π_1^et(X), π_1^et(Y)) is bijective (Corollary 1.6).
items.locator: Theorem 1.5 and Corollary 1.6, p. 819; proof on p. 847
items.note: Hoshi proves a similar statement in dimension ≤ 4 by other methods.

items.name: Lemma 6.3 and Corollary 1.7: anabelian Zariski neighbourhoods (Grothendieck's prediction)
items.statement: Every point of a smooth geometrically connected variety over an infinite perfect field has a fundamental system of Zariski-open strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods (Lemma 6.3). Hence every point of a smooth geometrically connected variety over k finitely generated over Q has a basis of Zariski neighbourhoods that are anabelian: k-isomorphisms between any two correspond bijectively to outer G_k-isomorphisms of their étale fundamental groups (Corollary 1.7).
items.locator: Corollary 1.7, p. 819; Lemma 6.3, pp. 847–849; proof as corrected by E7
items.note: First remove the hyperplanes x_i = 0, x_i = x_0 to embed in (P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞})^n, then use SGA 4 XI 3.3 and induction on dimension.

items.name: Constant fields and divisible elements
items.statement: For a geometrically connected variety X over k, k is the maximal subfield of H^0(X, O_X) (Tamagawa, Lemma 4.2), so scheme isomorphisms X → Y induce isomorphisms of constant fields; a finitely generated extension field of Q has no nontrivial divisible elements in its multiplicative group.

items.name: Theorem 1.8 and Theorem 7.1: the absolute version
items.statement: For k, ℓ finitely generated over Q and X/k, Y/ℓ smooth geometrically connected varieties embeddable in products of hyperbolic curves, Isom_Schemes(X, Y) → Isom_Ho(pro-ss)(X_et, Y_et) is a split injection with a functorial retraction, and a bijection if X and Y are strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods.
items.note: G_k is recovered as the quotient of π_1^et(X) by its maximal finitely generated closed normal subgroup; Pop's theorem identifies the base fields, and Theorems 1.2 and 1.5 apply over a fixed identification.

items.name: Theorem 7.2: varieties that are not geometrically connected
items.statement: For k finitely generated over Q and smooth k-varieties X, Y each of whose connected components embeds in a product of hyperbolic curves over its field of constants, Isom_k(X, Y) → Isom_{Ho(pro-ss)↓k_et}(X_et, Y_et) is a split injection with a functorial retraction, and a bijection if all components are strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods over their constant fields.
items.note: k-linearity of the constant-field isomorphism follows from Kummer theory: f_c^*(α) ≡ α mod (K^×)^n for all n.
